name: Purple Mountain Majesty
lede: Purple Mountain Majesty is a soft violet from Wikipedia's color lists, named for the phrase "purple mountain majesties" in the song "America the Beautiful," and not to be confused with Crayola's own crayon of a similar name.

sections.title: Not the Crayola crayon
sections.body:
This color, #9678B6, is listed on Wikipedia as "purple mountain majesty," a shade of lavender purple [1]. The name points to the lyric "for purple mountain majesties" in Katharine Lee Bates's 1893 hymn "America the Beautiful," describing the hazy violet of mountains seen from a distance, though our sources do not confirm the color was picked to match that line [1][2].

Crayola sells its own crayon under the related name "Purple Mountains' Majesty," introduced in 1993 at #8071B4, a bluer, darker violet than this one [3]. The two are often confused online, but they are different swatches from different sources [1][3]. The nearest named colors on file are [[middle-blue-purple]], [[middle-blue-purple]], [[orchid-purple]] and [[pearl-violet]], at 4.1, 4.4, 5.1 and 5.1 ΔE [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive carries this exact violet covering at least one percent of its canvas, as photographed [4]. That says more about the thinness of pure violets in old paint than about the color itself: aged varnish and fading pull violets toward brown and grey long before a photograph is taken [4]. The word itself, by contrast, has only grown in print since the 1950s, tracking tourism and patriotic songbooks rather than any painter's palette [4].
